content.title: About
content.content: Fish sauce is a liquid seasoning made by fermenting fish (usually anchovies) with salt. It is a staple in Southeast Asian cuisines, providing a distinctive salty‑umami flavor and aroma to dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Thai fish sauce, called “nam pla,” has been produced for over 200 years.
Vietnamese fish sauce (“nuoc mam”) is often aged up to two years to deepen its flavor.
Fermentation releases amino acids, especially glutamate, which is responsible for the umami taste.
Fish sauce can be light (milder) or dark (more intense) depending on the length of aging.
In some countries the sauce is considered a national product and enjoys protected geographical status.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Fermentation retains a portion of fish protein, which is easily digestible.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Fish sauce provides vitamin B12, essential for nerve function and blood formation.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermented foods may promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many sauces, fish sauce contains virtually no fat.

items.title: Enhances flavor without extra salt
items.content: Because of its strong umami profile, a small amount can replace a larger quantity of salt in recipes.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Fish sauce is very salty; people with hypertension should limit its use.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may experience reactions after consuming the sauce.

items.title: Histamine levels
items.content: Fermented products can contain histamine, which may trigger headaches in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Product quality
items.content: Low‑quality sauces may contain additives, artificial flavors, and preservatives.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add fish sauce to marinades, sauces, soups, salads, and stir‑fries. A few drops can boost the flavor of soy sauce, curry pastes, or tomato sauces. It is often combined with lime, garlic, and sugar to create classic Asian dressings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fish sauce in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator after opening. Properly stored, it retains its flavor for up to a year. Discard if it becomes cloudy, changes color, or develops an off smell.
